samples.question: The board carries small coloured squares that are decoration and mean nothing. Only three things decide the answer: two white panels with dark borders, and one small square that is drawn inside a thick black frame on the bare board. The framed square is the TOKEN; its own colour is red, blue, green or purple, and no other square on the bare board has a black frame. Each white panel holds exactly four rows. In one panel, called the TAG panel, every row has a coloured block on its left and a group of black dots on its right; its four block colours are red, blue, green and purple in some order. In the other panel, called the SLOT panel, every row has a group of black dots on its left and a coloured block on its right; its four block colours are orange, teal, pink and brown in some order. Inside each panel separately the four dot groups hold one, two, three and four dots, each count appearing exactly once. Read the answer in two steps and in this order. First, in the TAG panel find the row whose coloured block is the same colour as the TOKEN, and note how many dots that row holds. Second, in the SLOT panel find the row holding that same number of dots. That SLOT row is the OUTPUT row. Dot counts are the only link between the two panels: do not pair rows by their position in the panel, by how near they are drawn to each other, or by colour, and the TOKEN's colour never appears inside the SLOT panel. What colour is the coloured block of the OUTPUT row? Answer orange, teal, pink or brown.
